text: Last lesson of the chapter. The Analytics pane adds real analytical power to a chart you've already built — no new visual required.

The most common addition: a reference line. Select a line type, Add, name it, pick the measure — here, an average line labeled Average sales. Min, max, median, and percentile lines all work the same way.

With real time-series data, Forecast projects future values from historical trend. The shaded band is the confidence interval — how certain the prediction is, widening the further out it goes. Forecasting and anomaly detection both need a line chart with genuine dates to work from.

And beyond the Analytics pane, a few AI-powered visuals worth recognizing: decomposition tree for drilling across dimensions in any order, key influencers for surfacing what actually affects a result, smart narrative for automatically writing up the takeaway in plain language.
Ten lessons, one report full of the right visuals, properly filtered, properly connected. Next up: Chapter Eight, Dashboard Design and Storytelling.
